text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London showed little movement during later afternoon trading although the turnover was boosted to 4,510 lots as players rolled out of the near August position ahead of its expiry later this month. August ended down $0.10 from Friday closing at $319.10 per tonne.
Traders said there was very little going on in physicals to give fresh direction to the market and technically it was finely poised while trading around the pivotal $320 a tonne level.

Raw sugar futures in New York closed weaker and under support amid local selling and a lack of buying interest, market sources said. The benchmark October contract ended 0.12 cents/lb down at 11.06 cents/lb, having ranged from 11.20 to 11.06 cents/lb.
The rest of the board finished 0.02 to 0.10 cents/lb weaker. Technical resistance was pegged at Thursday's high of 11.22 cents basis the October contract, followed by 11.40 cents.

INDIA - Sugar production in May 1997 amounted to 490,200 tonnes, raw value, sharply down from last year's 1.655 million tonnes. This brought cumulative production in the first eight months of 1996/97 (October/May) up to 13.860 million tonnes compared to 16.780 million tonnes in the like period the previous year.

Total output in 1995/96 hit the record high of 17.883 million tonnes compared to 15.930 million tonnes in 1994/95. The figures so far hint at a seasonally adjusted total for 1996/97 of 14.8 million tonnes, raw value. Despite the sharp drop in production, India is unlikely to import sugar as local stocks are still very high.

PORTUGAL - Sugar imports in March 1997 amounted to 15,588 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 8,982 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first quarter of 1997 (January/March) up to 57,671 tonnes against 60,809 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1996 reached 310,625 tonnes, down from 312,542 tonnes in 1995.
Major countries of origin in 1997 were Mauritius with 15,160 tonnes raws against nil, Cuba with 12,997 tonnes against nil and Zambia with 12,208 tonnes, down from 13,512 tonnes.

CHINA - Imports continued at a sluggish pace with the May total reaching no more than 76,251 tonnes, sharply down from 137,502 tonnes imported in May 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first three quarters of 1996/97 (September/May) up to 633,264 tonnes, down from 1.482 million tonnes imported in the like period the previous year.

Total imports in 1995/96 reached 1.944 million tonnes compared to 2.907 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in 1996/97 were Australia with 279,793 tonnes raws against 351,995 tonnes, Cuba with 225,897 tonnes compared to 168,953 tonnes and Thailand with 63,382 tonnes, down from 486,479 tonnes. The largest supplier of white sugar in 1996/97 so far was South Korea with 29,122 tonnes compared to 24,405 tonnes.

Sugar exports in May 1997 reached 30,934 tonnes, down from 78,851 tonnes in May 1996. This brought cumulative exports in September/May 1996/97 up to 254,832 tonnes against 706,737 tonnes in 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/96 amounted to 830,203 tonnes, up from 540,004 tonnes in 1994/95.
Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Pakistan with 98,249 tonnes whites against nil, Saudi Arabia with 68,281 tonnes, up from 206,750 tonnes and Hong Kong with 29,071 tonnes
